question: At the moment an ordinary prefill runs out of device slots, is the approximate store still holding device bytes that the exact pressure path should have been able to reclaim?

supersedes: The earlier classification of the P6-4 S0/LRU rho2.0 cell as a genuine capacity limit is REFUTED by this measurement.
method: Poll /metrics every 0.4 s during the real P6-4 S0/LRU rho2.0 cell and keep the last sample before the server becomes unreachable.
findings: An approximate record holding 384 device tokens was still resident with leases=0, so it was freely evictable and was not evicted.
cross_store_reservation_failures_total was never incremented, so make_room(requester=exact) either was not invoked or returned committed. It never reported a failure.
832 device tokens are unaccounted for by either gauge while the allocator reports zero available and zero evictable.
The only dense fallback recorded came from reason=store_miss, not from a reservation failure.
candidate_mechanisms: evict_from_tree_cache only calls make_room when allocator.available_size() < num_tokens, so if available_size() disagrees with what alloc() can actually satisfy, the cross-store reclaim path is skipped entirely and the request dies without ever consulting the approximate store.
A second slot leak distinct from the admission-rejection leak already fixed, which would explain the 832 unaccounted tokens.
